engMnId: Beavers are often seen as pests because their dams flood roads and fields. Yet the wetlands they create filter water, store carbon and give homes to fish, birds and insects. What is the main idea of the passage?
Beavers cause problems but also create valuable wetlands.
Beavers build dams.
Roads sometimes flood.
Fish live in wetlands.
The passage weighs the problems beavers cause against the important benefits of their wetlands.

Many people think multitasking saves time. Research shows, however, that switching between tasks slows people down and leads to more mistakes than doing one thing at a time. What is the main idea of the passage?
Multitasking is less efficient than focusing on one task.
People like to save time.
Research is often surprising.
Mistakes are common.
Every detail supports the point that multitasking actually reduces efficiency.

The Inuit developed the qajaq, a lightweight boat made from driftwood or bone and sealskin. Its sleek design let hunters move silently and quickly through Arctic waters, and it later inspired the modern kayak. What is the main idea of the passage?
The Inuit qajaq was a brilliant design that shaped the modern kayak.
Sealskin is waterproof.
Arctic waters are cold.
Hunters need to be quiet.
The passage explains the qajaq's design and its lasting influence.

Food waste is a huge problem: Canadian households throw out millions of tonnes of edible food each year. Planning meals, storing food properly and using leftovers can cut that waste dramatically. What is the main idea of the passage?
Households waste a lot of food but can reduce it with simple habits.
Leftovers taste good.
Canada is a large country.
Food is expensive.
The passage presents a problem and practical ways to solve it.
Long before GPS, Polynesian navigators crossed thousands of kilometres of open ocean by reading the stars, ocean swells and the flight paths of birds. What is the main idea of the passage?
Polynesian navigators used natural clues to travel vast distances.
GPS is modern technology.
Birds can fly far.
The ocean is large.
Each detail shows how navigators used nature to find their way.

Some schools have replaced traditional grades with detailed written feedback. Supporters say students focus more on learning than on scores, while critics worry that families find the feedback harder to understand. What is the main idea of the passage?
Replacing grades with feedback has both supporters and critics.
Grades are numbers.
Families care about school.
Students like scores.
The passage presents both sides of the debate over replacing grades.

The monarch butterfly migrates up to 4,000 kilometres from Canada to Mexico. Remarkably, no single butterfly makes the round trip; it takes several generations to complete the cycle. What is the main idea of the passage?
Monarch migration is an extraordinary journey spread over generations.
Butterflies are orange.
Mexico is south of Canada.
Butterflies live short lives.
The passage stresses the remarkable, multi-generation nature of the migration.

Sleep is not just rest. During deep sleep, the brain sorts and stores memories, clears away waste products and repairs itself, which is why teenagers who sleep well often learn better. What is the main idea of the passage?
Sleep performs important work that helps the brain function and learn.
Teenagers are often tired.
The brain is complex.
Rest feels good.
The passage explains the active jobs the brain does during sleep.

When the Rideau Canal opened in 1832, it was built as a military supply route. Today it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and, in winter, one of the world's largest skating rinks. What is the main idea of the passage?
The Rideau Canal has changed from a military route to a beloved landmark.
Skating is popular.
The canal is old.
UNESCO protects sites.
The passage traces how the canal's purpose has changed over time.

Microbeads harmed waterways, which led Canada to ban them.
Face wash cleans skin.
Fish live in lakes.
Plastic is useful.
The passage explains the harm caused by microbeads and the resulting ban.

Volunteering can benefit the volunteer as much as the community. Studies link regular volunteering to lower stress, stronger friendships and a greater sense of purpose. What is the main idea of the passage?
Volunteering has real benefits for the volunteers themselves.
Communities need help.
Stress is common.
Friendships are important.
All the evidence points to how volunteering helps those who do it.

Shrinking glaciers threaten the water supply of communities downstream.
Glaciers are made of ice.
The Rockies are tall.
Summers are warm.
The passage links melting glaciers to their effects on people and nature downstream.

Some video games may build useful skills when played in moderation.
Video games are popular.
Teamwork is important.
Games waste time.
The passage argues that games can have benefits, contrary to a common belief.

The printing press transformed how knowledge spread.
Books were expensive.
The 1400s were long ago.
Reading is a skill.

Urban gardens offer many benefits beyond food.
Rooftops are high.
Vegetables are healthy.
Bees like flowers.
The passage lists the many benefits of urban gardens.

Sharks are far more threatened by humans than humans are by sharks.
Sharks have sharp teeth.
Swimming is dangerous.
Sharks live in oceans.
The passage contrasts shark attacks with the much larger human threat to sharks.
Libraries today do much more than lend books. Many offer free internet access, job-search help, language classes and spaces for community events. What is the main idea of the passage?
Modern libraries serve as wide-ranging community resources.
Libraries lend books.
Internet access is useful.
Language classes are fun.
The passage shows the many services libraries now provide.

Traditional Indigenous burning practices are being used to reduce wildfires today.
Forests have underbrush.
Wildfires are dangerous.
Grass grows back.
The passage connects long-standing Indigenous practice with modern wildfire prevention.
Learning a second language does more than help travellers. It can strengthen memory, improve focus and even delay signs of aging in the brain. What is the main idea of the passage?
Learning a second language benefits the brain.
Travel is fun.
Memory can fade.
Many languages exist.
Every detail describes a mental benefit of learning a language.

Fast fashion makes clothing cheap, but the low prices hide high costs: huge amounts of water and energy are used, and millions of garments end up in landfills each year. What is the main idea of the passage?
Cheap fast fashion carries serious environmental costs.
Clothes are affordable.
Landfills are large.
Fashion changes quickly.
The passage reveals the hidden environmental costs behind low prices.

Scientific study changed what people believed about the source of thought.
The heart pumps blood.
Anatomy is a science.
People think a lot.
The passage explains how scientific evidence overturned an old belief.

Engineers are working to make wind energy safer for wildlife.
Wind is free.
Birds migrate.
Turbines are tall.
The passage describes a problem with turbines and efforts to fix it.

I am writing to apply for the position of summer camp counsellor.
Hey, I wanna be a camp counsellor this summer.
So I heard you need camp counsellors?
I'm totally the right person for your camp job!
It states its purpose clearly in a formal, complete sentence.
Which text is most formal?
The library will be closed on Monday in observance of the holiday.
Library's closed Monday — holiday!
No library Monday, sorry!
The library's shut Monday 'cause of the holiday.
It avoids contractions and uses formal vocabulary such as in observance of.
Which text is most formal?
The author employs vivid imagery to convey the character's isolation.
The author uses lots of cool images to show the character's lonely.
The writer's pictures make you feel how lonely the guy is.
It's super obvious the character's lonely.
Its academic vocabulary suits a formal literary essay.
Which text is most formal?
Thank you for your prompt response to my inquiry.
Thanks for getting back to me so fast!
Wow, quick reply — thanks!
Cheers for answering my question.
Prompt response and inquiry are formal word choices.
Which text is most formal?
Participants should arrive fifteen minutes before the scheduled start time.
Show up 15 mins early, everyone.
Try to get there a bit early, OK?
Don't be late — come early!
It gives instructions in complete, impersonal sentences.
Which text is most formal?
Further research is required to confirm these results.
We gotta check this more.
Not sure this is right — more tests, maybe?
These results might be off, who knows.
It uses objective, precise language typical of formal writing.
Which text is most formal?
The municipality has approved funding for a new community centre.
The city's finally paying for a new community centre!
Guess what? New community centre coming!
They said yes to the community centre, yay.
Municipality and approved funding are formal terms.
Which text is most formal?
Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Got questions? Just text me.
Hit me up if you're confused.
Ask me if you need anything, no worries.
The inverted conditional and polite wording are formal.
Which text is most formal?
The committee unanimously endorsed the proposal.
Everybody on the committee liked the idea.
The committee was all in on the plan.
Yep, the committee said yes to it.
Unanimously endorsed is precise, formal vocabulary.
Which text is most formal?
Attendance at the assembly is mandatory for all students.
Everyone's gotta go to the assembly.
You can't skip the assembly, guys.
The assembly is a must — no excuses!
Mandatory and the impersonal tone make it formal.
Which text is most formal?
The data were collected over a period of six months.
We got the data over about six months.
It took like six months to get all the info.
Six months of data — phew!
It uses objective language and avoids casual expressions.
Which text is most formal?
Due to inclement weather, all outdoor activities have been cancelled.
It's gross out, so no outdoor stuff.
Rain's ruined everything — no outside fun.
Weather's bad, so we're staying in.
Inclement weather is a formal expression, and the sentence avoids slang.
Which text is most formal?
The museum's collection includes artifacts dating to the eighteenth century.
The museum's got some really old stuff.
There's tons of ancient junk at the museum.
You'll see super old things at the museum.
It uses precise nouns like artifacts and avoids vague slang.
Which text is most formal?
I respectfully disagree with the council's decision.
The council's decision is totally dumb.
No way, the council messed up.
I'm so not okay with what the council did.
It expresses disagreement politely and formally.
Which text is most formal?
Employees are reminded to log out of their computers at the end of each shift.
Don't forget to log off, team!
Log out before you leave, OK?
Seriously, log out when you're done.
It uses impersonal, complete phrasing suitable for a workplace notice.
Which text is most formal?
The results of the survey suggest that most residents favour the new bylaw.
Most people seem to like the new rule, I think.
Looks like everybody's into the new bylaw.
Survey says: people dig the bylaw.
It uses objective wording and precise terms like residents and bylaw.
Which text is most formal?
Kindly ensure that all forms are signed prior to submission.
Sign your forms before handing them in, please.
Make sure you sign the stuff first.
Don't forget to sign — duh!
Kindly ensure and prior to submission are formal phrases.
engAuPu: "Be sure to tighten each lug nut in a star pattern to keep the wheel evenly seated." Who is the most likely audience?
The technical car-repair instructions suit people working on a car.
"Once upon a time, a little fox lost his red mitten in the snow." Who is the most likely audience?
The simple fairy-tale language and subject suit young children.
"The quadratic formula gives the roots of any equation of the form ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0." Who is the most likely audience?
The mathematical content is written for students learning algebra.
"Our new running shoe cushions every step — get 20% off this weekend only!" What is the purpose?
To persuade readers to buy shoes
To explain how shoes are made
To describe the history of running
The discount and praise are meant to convince readers to buy.
A brochure lists the opening hours, ticket prices and parking options for a science centre. What is the purpose?
It gives practical facts that visitors need.
"Dear Council Members, I urge you to install a crosswalk on Elm Street before someone is hurt." What is the purpose?
To persuade the council to act
To inform students about traffic laws
The writer urges the council to take a specific action.
"Patients should take one tablet twice daily with food and avoid alcohol." Who is the most likely audience?
The dosage instructions are written for patients using the medicine.
A humorous story describes a cat that keeps stealing socks from the laundry basket. What is the purpose?
To persuade people to buy socks
The funny story is meant mainly to amuse.
"In this lab, you will measure the pH of five household liquids and record your observations." Who is the most likely audience?
Lab instructions about pH are written for science students.
A government website explains how to apply for a passport and what documents are needed. What is the purpose?
To inform people about a process
To persuade people not to travel
It explains steps and requirements, which informs readers.
"Join the Green Team! Together we can make our school waste-free. Sign up in Room 112." Who is the most likely audience?
The call to join a school club is aimed at students.
"Preheat the oven to 180 °C and whisk the eggs until frothy." Who is the most likely audience?
The cooking steps are written for someone baking.
An editorial argues that the city should extend library hours for teens studying for exams. What is the purpose?
To persuade readers to support longer hours
To describe how books are printed
An editorial gives an opinion and tries to win support.
"Shareholders will receive a dividend of $0.45 per share on March 31." Who is the most likely audience?
Dividends and shareholders are terms for company investors.
A diary entry describes how the writer felt on the first day at a new school. What is the purpose?
To give directions to the school
To persuade parents to choose the school
Diary entries mainly record and express the writer's own experiences.
"Coaches must certify that all players have completed concussion training before the season begins." Who is the most likely audience?
The rule speaks directly to coaches.
A pamphlet explains the warning signs of a stroke and when to call 911. What is the purpose?
To inform the public about health
To persuade people to buy medicine
It gives important health facts so people can act.
"This sleek, waterproof jacket will keep you dry on every adventure — order now!" What is the purpose?
To persuade readers to buy a jacket
To entertain with a story about rain
To explain how waterproofing was invented
Praise and the call to order are persuasive techniques.
"Before landing, please return your seat to the upright position and fasten your seatbelt." Who is the most likely audience?
The instructions are announced to people on a plane.
A comic strip shows a penguin trying and failing to learn to fly. What is the purpose?
To persuade readers to visit Antarctica
A comic strip of this kind is meant to amuse.
"Claim the Canada Child Benefit by filing your tax return each year, even if you had no income." Who is the most likely audience?
The benefit information is aimed at those raising children.
A news report states how many centimetres of snow fell and which highways are closed. What is the purpose?
To inform readers about current conditions
To persuade people to move south
To entertain with a poem about snow
News reports present facts so readers know what is happening.
engSbOb: Passage A: "The hockey game ended 3–2 in overtime." Passage B: "The thrilling game ended in a nail-biting overtime win." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Words like thrilling and nail-biting reveal the writer's feelings.
Passage A: "This restaurant serves the most delicious pizza in town." Passage B: "The restaurant opened in 2019 and seats 60 people." Which passage is objective?
Passage B states only facts that can be checked.
Passage A: "The lazy council ignored residents again." Passage B: "The council voted 5–4 against the proposal." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Lazy is a judgment that shows the writer's opinion.
Passage A: "The museum holds over 10,000 artifacts." Passage B: "The museum's exhibits are fascinating and beautifully arranged." Which passage is objective?
Passage A gives a measurable fact without opinion.
Passage A: "The new phone has a 6.1-inch screen and a 12-megapixel camera." Passage B: "The new phone is a gorgeous, must-have gadget." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Gorgeous and must-have express the writer's opinion.
Passage A: "Temperatures reached 35 °C on Tuesday." Passage B: "Tuesday's heat was absolutely unbearable." Which passage is objective?
Passage A reports a measured temperature without judgment.
Passage A: "The film is a boring, overlong mess." Passage B: "The film runs two hours and forty minutes." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Boring and mess are opinion words.
Passage A: "The river flooded 200 homes in May." Passage B: "The terrible flood devastated the heartbroken town." Which passage is objective?
Passage A gives verifiable facts without emotional language.
Passage A: "The singer's voice is simply magical." Passage B: "The singer released her third album in June." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Magical expresses the writer's personal reaction.
Passage A: "The park has three trails and a picnic area." Passage B: "The park's trails total 12 kilometres." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Both passages state checkable facts without opinion words.
Passage A: "The novel is a dull, predictable story." Passage B: "Critics everywhere hated this awful novel." Which passage is objective?
Both passages use judgment words like dull and awful, so neither is objective.
Passage A: "The school added a new science lab this year." Passage B: "Enrolment rose by 8% from last year." Which passage is objective?
Passage A: "The mayor's brilliant plan will save our city." Passage B: "The mayor's wasteful plan will bankrupt our city." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Brilliant and wasteful both reveal opinions.
Passage A: "Our team's heroic effort deserved a win." Passage B: "Our team outshot the opponents 30 to 18." Which passage is objective?
Passage B gives statistics without judgment.
Passage A: "The concert sold out in ten minutes." Passage B: "Fans were ecstatic to grab tickets to the best concert ever." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Ecstatic and best concert ever show strong opinion.
Passage A: "The bill would raise the minimum wage to $17 an hour." Passage B: "This shameful bill will destroy small businesses." Which passage is objective?
Passage A describes the bill factually.
Passage A: "Canada's population passed 40 million in 2023." Passage B: "The capital of Canada is Ottawa." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Both passages state facts without opinion.
Passage A: "The ridiculous new uniforms look terrible." Passage B: "The new uniforms are navy blue with white trim." Which passage is objective?
Passage B describes the uniforms without judgment.
Passage A: "The speech lasted 45 minutes." Passage B: "The speaker droned on for an endless 45 minutes." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Droned on and endless show the writer's negative opinion.
Passage A: "The bakery's croissants are heavenly." Passage B: "The bakery's owner is a genius." Which passage is objective?
Heavenly and genius are both opinions, so neither passage is objective.
Passage A: "The study surveyed 1,200 students across Ontario." Passage B: "About 60% of respondents reported sleeping less than eight hours." Which passage is objective?
Both passages report facts from the study without opinion.
Passage A: "The selfish neighbours refused to help." Passage B: "The neighbours declined to sign the petition." Which passage uses a subjective tone?
Selfish is a judgment that reveals the writer's feelings.
engPOV: What point of view is this? I clutched the map and wondered if we would ever find the trail.
The narrator uses I and describes their own thoughts.
What point of view is this? You step onto the ice and feel it creak beneath your boots.
The narrator addresses the reader as you.
What point of view is this? Marcus stared at the test, wondering whether he had studied the right chapter. The teacher smiled at the class, and Marcus wished he knew what she was thinking.
The narrator uses he and reveals only Marcus's thoughts.
What point of view is this? Elena hoped no one noticed her shaking hands, while across the room Raj secretly worried that his own speech would be worse.
The narrator reveals the private thoughts of both Elena and Raj.
What point of view is this? We huddled under the tarp as the rain hammered the tent.
We shows the narrator is part of the story.
What point of view is this? You open the envelope slowly, afraid of what it might say.
The story puts the reader in the action using you.
What point of view is this? Priya listened to the wind and felt sure someone was outside. She could not guess what her brother, asleep in the next room, was dreaming about.
Only Priya's thoughts are shown, and the narrator says she cannot know her brother's.
What point of view is this? The captain believed the storm would pass, the crew feared it would not, and the passengers had no idea how much danger they were in.
The narrator knows the thoughts and knowledge of many characters.
What point of view is this? My grandmother taught me to bake bannock when I was seven.
My and me show a narrator telling their own story.
What point of view is this? Oliver dreaded the dentist appointment. He kept checking the clock, sure it was moving faster than usual.
The narrator uses he and stays inside Oliver's mind.
What point of view is this? The wolf thought only of food, the rabbit thought only of escape, and the old owl, watching from above, knew how the chase would end.
The narrator reveals what several different characters think.
What point of view is this? You hear footsteps behind you, so you walk a little faster.
The reader is addressed directly as you.
What point of view is this? I never told anyone what I saw in the attic that night.
The narrator speaks as I about their own experience.
What point of view is this? Jada was certain her friends had forgotten her birthday. She trudged home, unaware of anything waiting for her.
The narrator follows only Jada's thoughts and what she knows.
What point of view is this? Each family on the street privately believed theirs was the happiest, and each was secretly wrong in a different way.
The narrator knows the private beliefs of every family.
What point of view is this? Our canoe tipped just as we rounded the bend.
Our and we show the narrator is a character.
What point of view is this? You reach for the doorknob, but something makes you hesitate.
The narrator speaks directly to you.
What point of view is this? Kofi wondered why the coach looked so serious. He had no idea that the team was about to be told big news.
Only Kofi's thoughts are revealed, and the narrator keeps to what he knows.
What point of view is this? The mother worried about the bills, the father worried about his job, and their son worried only about tomorrow's hockey game.
The narrator reveals the separate worries of three characters.
What point of view is this? I could feel my heart pounding as my name was called.
The narrator uses I and my to describe their own feelings.
What point of view is this? Sam studied the old photograph, trying to remember the day it was taken.
The narrator uses third-person pronouns and shows only Sam's thoughts.
What point of view is this? You never expected the quiet new student to become your closest friend.
The narrator addresses the reader directly with you.
engFgEh: Which figure of speech is this? The store is having a pre-owned car sale.
Pre-owned is a gentler way of saying used.
Which figure of speech is this? I've told you a thousand times to close the door.
A thousand times is an obvious exaggeration for emphasis.
Which figure of speech is this? It was an open secret that she was moving away.
Open and secret are contradictory words placed side by side.
Which figure of speech is this? Less is more.
The statement seems contradictory but expresses a truth about simplicity.
Which figure of speech is this? My grandfather is a senior citizen.
Senior citizen is a polite way of saying old person.
Which figure of speech is this? This backpack weighs more than an elephant.
No backpack truly outweighs an elephant; it is exaggeration.
Which figure of speech is this? The pretty ugly sweater made everyone laugh.
Pretty ugly joins two opposite ideas in one phrase.
Which figure of speech is this? You have to be cruel to be kind.
It seems self-contradictory but reveals that hard choices can help someone.
Which figure of speech is this? The soldiers were killed by friendly fire.
Friendly fire softens the harsh fact of being shot by one's own side.
Which figure of speech is this? I'm so tired I could sleep for a year.
Sleeping for a year is an extreme exaggeration.
Which figure of speech is this? The meeting produced an original copy of the report.
Original and copy contradict each other.
Which figure of speech is this? The beginning of the end had arrived.
Beginning and end seem contradictory but express a truth about a turning point.
Which figure of speech is this? The custodian is a sanitation engineer.
Sanitation engineer is a more flattering term for a cleaner.
Which figure of speech is this? The line at the bakery was a mile long.
A mile-long line exaggerates how long the wait was.
Which figure of speech is this? Their argument ended in a peaceful war of words.
Peaceful and war are contradictory terms combined for effect.
Which figure of speech is this? The only constant is change.
It sounds contradictory, yet it truthfully says change never stops.
Which figure of speech is this? The company let go of fifty workers.
Let go is a softer way of saying fired.
Which figure of speech is this? My little brother cried an ocean of tears.
An ocean of tears is a huge exaggeration.
Which figure of speech is this? We heard a quiet roar from the distant waterfall.
Quiet and roar are opposites placed together.
Which figure of speech is this? If you want to save time, slow down.
Slowing down to save time seems contradictory but can be true because you make fewer mistakes.
Which figure of speech is this? She's a little thin on top these days.
Thin on top is a gentle way of saying bald.
Which figure of speech is this? He ran faster than the speed of light.
No one can run faster than light; it is exaggeration.
engFgRv: Which figure of speech is this? O moon, why do you hide behind the clouds tonight?
The speaker addresses the moon, which cannot answer.
Which figure of speech is this? We will not tire, we will not falter, we will not fail.
The phrase we will not is repeated at the start of each clause.
Which figure of speech is this? That was a living nightmare.
Living and nightmare combine contrasting ideas in a short phrase.
Which figure of speech is this? Speech is silver, but silence is golden.
Speech and silence are contrasting ideas set in balanced clauses.
Which figure of speech is this? Scoring 98% on the exam wasn't too bad.
Calling an excellent score not too bad deliberately downplays it.
Which figure of speech is this? My parents will kill me if I'm late again.
The exaggeration emphasizes how upset the parents will be.
Which figure of speech is this? Our cat was put to sleep last spring.
Put to sleep is a gentle way of saying the cat was euthanized.
Which figure of speech is this? I must be cruel only to be kind.
Being cruel to be kind seems contradictory but expresses a truth.
Which figure of speech is this? Every day we read, every day we learn, every day we grow.
Every day is repeated at the beginning of successive clauses.
Which figure of speech is this? Death, be not proud.
The speaker addresses death as though it could listen.
Which figure of speech is this? It's a small step for one person, a giant leap for a community.
Small step and giant leap are balanced opposites.
Which figure of speech is this? The Sahara is a bit warm in July.
Calling the scorching desert a bit warm downplays the extreme heat.
Which figure of speech is this? This homework will take me a century.
A century is an exaggeration for a long time.
Which figure of speech is this? The army officially withdrew, though people called it a strategic retreat.
Strategic retreat is a softer term that disguises a defeat.
Which figure of speech is this? The silence spoke volumes.
Silence speaking seems impossible but conveys a truth about meaning.
Which figure of speech is this? The comedian's act was seriously funny.
Seriously and funny are contradictory words joined together.
Which figure of speech is this? Oh, stubborn old car, please start just this once!
The speaker addresses an object that cannot respond.
Which figure of speech is this? Not that the losing streak bothered the fans much — they only booed for three hours.
Saying it didn't bother them much downplays obvious anger.
Which figure of speech is this? Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country.
The two clauses reverse and contrast the same ideas.
Which figure of speech is this? We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields.
We shall fight is repeated at the start of each clause.
Which figure of speech is this? The janitor is now called a custodial engineer.
Custodial engineer is a more dignified-sounding term for janitor.
Which figure of speech is this? I'm drowning in a sea of homework.
The exaggeration stresses how much homework there is.
engLTD: Which literary device is shown? The scarlet maple leaves rustled against the cool, blue October sky.
Vivid details of colour, sound and temperature appeal to the senses.
Which literary device is shown? A lifeguard who cannot swim.
You would expect a lifeguard to swim, so the opposite is ironic.
Which literary device is shown? Before the trip, the old sailor warns, "Not everyone who sails that strait comes back."
The warning hints that danger will come later.
Which literary device is shown? In the middle of the game, the story jumps back to the day the player first laced up skates.
The story moves back in time to an earlier event.
Which literary device is shown? A broken chain on the prisoner's wrist stands for his new freedom.
The broken chain represents the idea of freedom.
Which literary device is shown? The smell of fresh bread and warm cinnamon filled the tiny kitchen.
Details of smell and warmth create a sensory picture.
Which literary device is shown? A traffic-safety expert gets a speeding ticket.
The outcome is the opposite of what we would expect from a safety expert.
Which literary device is shown? The heroine notices a crack in the dam days before the heavy rains begin.
The crack hints at a disaster to come.
Which literary device is shown? As she holds the faded letter, she remembers the summer her father left.
The scene returns to an earlier time in the character's life.
Which literary device is shown? A wilting rose on the windowsill represents a fading friendship.
The rose stands for something beyond itself: the friendship.
Which literary device is shown? Thunder cracked like a whip, and icy rain stung their cheeks.
Sound and touch details help readers feel the storm.
Which literary device is shown? A famous chef can't boil an egg at home.
It is the opposite of what we expect from a skilled chef.
Which literary device is shown? The new student glances nervously at the locked door no one is allowed to open.
The forbidden door hints it will matter later.
Which literary device is shown? The chapter returns to the night of the fire twenty years earlier.
The narrative goes back to past events.
Which literary device is shown? A lit candle in the window shows the family still has hope.
Which literary device is shown? The glossy black crow cawed hoarsely from the frost-covered fence.
Details of sight and sound create a vivid picture.
Which literary device is shown? The marriage counsellor files for divorce.
The result is the opposite of what we would expect from a marriage counsellor.
Which literary device is shown? Early in the story, the father checks the old rifle on the wall and says it still works.
Mentioning the rifle hints that it will be used later.
Which literary device is shown? Lying in the hospital bed, he relives the moment of the accident.
The story interrupts the present to show an earlier event.
Which literary device is shown? The caged bird in the story represents the girl's trapped life.
The caged bird stands for the girl's lack of freedom.
Which literary device is shown? Sticky, sweet juice dripped down our chins as we bit into the peaches.
Taste and touch details make the moment vivid.
Which literary device is shown? The weather forecaster forgets his umbrella and is caught in a downpour.
The person who predicts weather is unprepared for it, which is ironic.
engShS: Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Every afternoon, Ayesha left half her lunch on the bench by the library. One day she stayed to watch, and a boy from her class, who never ate in the cafeteria, slipped the sandwich into his bag. The next day she packed two sandwiches. What can be inferred about Ayesha?
She is quietly generous and wants to help without embarrassing him.
She is trying to lose weight.
She dislikes the boy and is testing him.
She forgets to eat her lunch.
Packing an extra sandwich after seeing his need shows quiet kindness.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). The old bridge creaked as Jonah stepped onto it. Halfway across, a board snapped. He froze, then remembered his grandfather's advice: "Move slowly, keep your weight low." Crouching, he inched forward until his boots touched solid ground. What is the main conflict in the story?
Jonah against the dangerous bridge
Jonah against his grandfather
Jonah against a rival
Jonah against his town
The struggle is with the physical danger of the bridge, a person-versus-nature conflict.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Clara laughed at the new girl's handmade sweater. That evening, her mother pulled out a box of sweaters she had knitted for Clara when she was small. Clara held one for a long time and said nothing. What is Clara most likely feeling?
Regretful about the way she treated the new girl
Proud of her own clothes
Angry at her mother
Bored by the sweaters
Remembering her mother's handmade gifts makes her see her cruelty in a new light.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). For years Mr. Petrov's corner store had the only fresh bread in town. When a big supermarket opened, the crowds disappeared. Then, one snowy morning, the supermarket's power failed, and a long line formed outside Mr. Petrov's door. He smiled and simply said, "Good morning." What theme does the story suggest?
Loyalty and patience can be rewarded in unexpected ways.
Big stores are always better.
Snow ruins businesses.
People should never shop locally.
The small store's steady presence is finally appreciated when it is needed.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Nadia's hands shook as she read the acceptance letter. She read it again. Then she ran down the hallway, shouting her brother's name, and they both jumped until the floor shook. Why does the author repeat that Nadia read the letter again?
To show she could hardly believe the good news
To show she could not read well
To suggest the letter was confusing
To show she was bored
Rereading shows her disbelief before the joy sinks in.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Every spring, Grandma Lu planted marigolds along the fence. The year she moved into a care home, the family forgot. In June, though, orange flowers appeared anyway — seeds from last year had scattered. Her granddaughter brought her a photo, and Grandma Lu laughed for the first time in weeks. What do the marigolds most likely symbolize?
Grandma Lu's lasting influence on her family
The family's carelessness
The end of summer
A dangerous weed
The flowers returning on their own suggest her care continues even after she leaves.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Theo always took the shortcut through the woods. Tonight, though, the path seemed darker, and a branch snapped behind him. He walked faster, then laughed when a raccoon waddled out of the bushes. How does the author build suspense?
By describing darkness and an unexplained sound
By using a cheerful narrator
By listing facts about raccoons
By telling the ending first
The dark path and mysterious snap make readers feel tense before the harmless reveal.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Hana practised her speech in front of the mirror every night. On the day of the assembly, the microphone died. Without missing a beat, she stepped forward and spoke louder, and the audience leaned in. What trait does Hana show?
Adaptability under pressure
Laziness
Shyness that stops her
Carelessness
She adjusts calmly when the microphone fails.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Every evening, Ravi's father came home late, tired and quiet. Ravi thought he didn't care. Then Ravi found a notebook in the car filled with his hockey scores, each game carefully recorded. What does Ravi most likely realize?
His father has been paying attention all along.
His father wants to quit his job.
His father dislikes hockey.
The notebook belongs to someone else.
The detailed records reveal his father's hidden interest and love.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). "We'll never win," Ben grumbled as the rain poured on the soccer field. Mira tightened her ponytail. "Then let's lose trying." She ran back into position. How do Ben and Mira differ?
Ben is discouraged, while Mira is determined.
Ben is determined, while Mira gives up.
Both are eager to quit.
Both are excited about the rain.
Ben's complaint contrasts with Mira's decision to keep playing.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Sofia found the injured sparrow in the snow and carried it home in her mitten. For a week she fed it seeds and water. When it finally flew from her window, she cried, then smiled. What is the best theme?
Caring for something sometimes means letting it go.
Birds are dangerous pets.
Winter is cruel to everyone.
Crying shows weakness.
Her mixed tears and smile show that releasing the bird is an act of love.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). The village elders said the river spirit punished anyone who fished at night. Kiona did not believe them, until the night her boat drifted silently into a whirlpool she had never seen in daylight. What is the most likely purpose of the elders' warning?
To foreshadow the danger Kiona later faces
To show the elders are foolish
To explain how to fish
To describe the village's history
The warning hints at the danger that comes true later in the story.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Mateo told everyone his family was going to Paris for March break. On the first day back, when friends asked for photos, he changed the subject and stared at his shoes. What can be inferred?
Mateo probably did not actually go to Paris.
Mateo lost his camera on the plane.
Mateo loved Paris too much to talk about it.
Mateo's friends are not interested.
Avoiding the question and looking down suggest he exaggerated or made up the trip.

She notices small changes others overlook.
She cannot think of anything else to paint.
She dislikes the lake.
She wants to stop painting.

He grows closer to his sister.
He becomes angry at the storm.

Without his usual distraction, he spends time with and bonds with his sister.

He is kinder than his grumpy manner suggests.
He wants to keep the kite.
He is afraid of ladders.
He hates all children.
His helpful action contrasts with his gruff reputation.

Her joy at winning versus her sympathy for her friend
Emma against the director
Emma against a storm
Emma against her parents

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). The sign on the bakery said "Closed Forever." Nostalgic and bittersweet
Terrifying
Cheerful and silly
Angry
Fond memories mixed with loss create a bittersweet mood.

Amir has begun to feel proud of his name.
Amir wants to change his name.

Amir is angry at the teacher.

They secretly won the game.

They did not care about the game.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Iris kept the seashell from her mother's last trip to the coast. Whenever she felt lonely at university, she held it to her ear and listened to the faint rush of the waves. What does the seashell represent for Iris?
A comforting connection to her mother and home
A science experiment
Something she plans to sell
Her fear of the ocean
She turns to the shell when lonely, showing it links her to her mother.

Read the short story (an original story written for LearnAce). Diego practised his free throws every night under the streetlight. His older brother teased him. Steady effort pays off and can change how others see you.
Older brothers are always mean.
Luck matters more than practice.
Streetlights help athletes.
Diego's nightly practice leads to success and wins his brother's respect.
